Tips for the Arab traveler when visiting: Tips for Arab travellers visiting Kazakhstan
To ensure an enjoyable and comfortable t: To ensure an enjoyable and comfortable trip to Kazakhstan, here are some useful tips for Arab travellers:
Kazakhstan is a Muslim-majority country,: Kazakhstan is a Muslim-majority country where conservative customs and traditions are valued. It is advisable to wear modest clothing, especially when visiting mosques and religious places. Greeting older people with respect and not photographing people without their permission are much appreciated.
Kazakh is the official language, and Rus: Kazakh is the official language, and Russian is widely spoken and used as a lingua franca, especially in major cities. English may not be widely spoken outside major hotels and the main tourist areas. It is a good idea to learn some basic phrases in Russian or Kazakh (such as “hello”, “thank you”, “how much?”), and translation apps can be very helpful.
Since Kazakhstan is a Muslim-majority co: Since Kazakhstan is a Muslim-majority country, finding halal food is relatively easy, especially in local restaurants and markets. You can ask whether food is halal when shopping or in restaurants. Traditional Kazakh dishes such as beshbarmak and lagman are often prepared with halal meat.
It is preferable to drink bottled water: It is best to drink bottled water rather than tap water, especially outside major cities, to be on the safe side.
The local currency is the Kazakhstani te: The local currency is the Kazakhstani tenge (KZT). Major foreign currencies (such as US dollars and euros) can be exchanged easily at banks and authorised exchange offices in major cities. Credit cards are also commonly used in major hotels, restaurants and modern shops, but it is a good idea to carry some cash for small purchases and local markets.
Kazakhstan is generally a safe country f: Kazakhstan is generally a safe country for travellers. However, it is advisable to take the usual precautions, such as keeping personal belongings safe, avoiding secluded areas at night and not displaying large amounts of money openly. Using licensed taxis or ride-hailing apps is recommended.

Wi-Fi is available in most hotels, cafes and restaurants.
